The faeries that do live there include High Fae and various Lesser Fae species. Many of its High Fae inhabitants are described as having pale or ruddy skin, as well as black eyes. Their eyes appear soulless and cold from centuries of indulging in cruelty, even those of the nameless courtiers who reside at the King of Hybern's castle.

No humans reside in Hybern, as it is fully north of the Wall. The political power was focused on one king instead of being split between several High Lords. The king had a number of Commanders. Two of his elite hunters were the Ravens, a pair of High Fae who would be sent to retrieve things the King of Hybern wanted.

The symbol of Hybern is unknown but a picture of Hybern showed a small crown in the center. As the same map showed Prythian's courts and included their symbols, this may be Hybern's.

entries.name: Velaris
entries.content:
Velaris, also known as the Court of Dreams and the City of Starlight, is a hidden city on the western side of the Night Court of Prythian. Velaris is built like a crust atop rolling, steep hills. The hills are flanked by a broad, winding river the color of the deepest sapphire, the Sidra River, that snakes across the landscape into the sea. The Sidra River has ships with sails of varying shapes placed along it permanently, making it navigable. At the northern edge of Velaris, curved to where the river bent toward them and flowed into their shadows, tower, like eternal guardians of the city, a wall of flat-topped mountains of red stone. Their middle and larger peak has holes and windows built in the uppermost part of it, in fact, there is where the House of Wind, can be found. To the north are different kinds of mountains that surround the city across the river, which are a range of sharp peaks comparable to fish teeth cut through city's hills from the sea beyond.

The city's buildings are crafted out of white marble, warm sandstone, and the same red stone of the flat-topped mountains that can be found on the northern edge of the city. Many quarters of Velaris are full of townhouses with green copper roofs and white chimneys.

In Velaris many shops can be found with delicate tables and chairs scattered outside their cheery fronts, restaurants like the Restaurant where the Inner Circle go dining, and nightclubs like the Rita's. Many of these buildings are heated by warming spells.

Velaris has four market squares called Palaces, two on the southern side of the Sidra River and two on the northern side. We know the name of only three of the four squares: the Palace of Thread and Jewels and the Palace of Bone and Salt that sell respectively jewels and food and are positioned on the southern side of the Sidra River, and, the Palace of Hoof and Leaf positioned on the northern side of the Sidra River and twin square to the Palace of Bone and Salt. They are white-stoned squares flanked by Tehran pillars supporting the carved and painted buildings that watch over them, and provide a covered walkway beneath the shops built into the street level.

What Velaris is most known for is the artists' quarter, called the Rainbow of Velaris, home of performing artists, like the musicians, the dancers, and the actors. It is a brightly painted pocket of the city, built atop one of the hills that flowed right to the river's edge. In the Rainbow of Velaris there are around a hundred galleries, supply stores, potters' compounds, sculpture gardens, and anything in between. In this quarter there is a building with a golden top, the most famous of the five main theaters in the city. There are also other smaller theaters and an amphitheater on the sea cliff.

entries.name: Night Court
entries.content: The Night Court is one of the seven Courts of Prythian and one of the three Solar Courts. It is divided into two sub-Courts, the Court of Nightmares, and the lesser known Court of Dreams. The Night Court is a mountainous court located at the northernmost region of Prythian, and boasts the largest amount of territory out of all the courts. The Night Court is bordered to the south by the Day Court. Though it is called "The Night Court," it follows the cycle of day and night, as every Solar Court does. However, the Night Court's nights are more breathtaking than those of any other Court.

entries.name: Day Court
entries.content: The Day Court is one of the seven courts of Prythian, and one of the three solar courts. The Day Court is bordered to the north by the Night Court, and to the south by the Dawn Court.

entries.name: Dawn Court
entries.content:
The Dawn Court is one of the seven courts in Prythian, and one of the three Solar Courts. The Dawn Court is bordered on the north by the Day Court and to the south by Under the Mountain and the Winter Court. Its sky is cobalt and tinged by the rose remnants of sunrise long into the day, the edges of soft clouds gild with golden light. The air has lingering dewy freshness in the air. It is a lush, eternal countryside rich with the weight of summer upon it.

Dawn's territory is set in small cities that specialized in tinkering, clockwork, and clever things. The towns were red-roofed villages with sparkling rivers.

entries.name: Spring Court
entries.content:
The Spring Court is one of the seven Courts of Prythian and one of the four Seasonal Courts. The Spring Court is a land of rolling green hills, lush forests, and clear, bottomless lakes. Magic didn’t just abound in the bumps and the hollows – it grew there. To the south, the Court borders the Wall and likewise the Mortal Realm. Its northern borders are the Summer Court and the Autumn Court.

While the Spring Court boasts no cities, a large village is located close to the High Lord’s estate, less than five miles away. It is seen as the much "calmer" ones to the benevolence of the Fae compared to Summer. The fae of this court are generally polite and bright-eyed. They also have blossoming curiosity. The Spring Court is strongest during the ends of winter and throughout the spring season, despite the Summer Court having reigned. These fae are peppy, quiet, seductive, emotional, and vernal obviously. The epitome of spring.

entries.name: Summer Court
entries.content:
The Summer Court is one of the seven Courts of Prythian and one of the four Seasonal Courts. The Summer Court is bordered to south by the Spring Court. Its eastern border is the Autumn Court, and the northern border is the Winter Court.

The Summer Court boasts four cities, one of which is the city of Adriata where the High Lord of Summer spends the last weeks of winter and first weeks of spring. A palace is built atop a mountain-island in the heart of a half-moon bay. The city circles the island on three sides and spreads toward the sparkling sea. The fae of this court are generally considered more polite or mannered, albeit they are still very capable of cruelty (but will be more hush-hush, or subtle about it). The Summer Court has free reign over summer solstice and spring equinox months, and are strongest during that time. Needless to say, the fae of this court are frivolous, venereal, hot-headed and what have you. They are the epitome of summer.

entries.name: Autumn Court
entries.content: The Autumn Court is one of the seven courts of Prythian, and a Seasonal Court. It is known to be beautiful, cutthroat, and highly competitive, a court of foxes. The woods of the Autumn Court look like a jewelry box, a latticework of red, gold, brown, and green. The colors are so vivid that it's hard not to gawk and gape. Surrounding the forests of the Autumn Court are farmlands and fields, inhabited by the Lesser Faeries who work the land. It is a land of fertile valleys and jade streams that end in steep foothills that leaped into gray, snowcapped mountains mark the start of the shared range with the Winter Court to the north. It limits to the west with the Summer Court, while to the south is the Spring Court. The fae of this court are generally the ones doing the "dirty work" and "trooping". However, these fae can have much nicer sides than any of the Fae and return great favors. The Autumn Court is strongest during the ends of summer and throughout the autumn season. These fae are strong, mystique, eerie, ravishing all the same, and devious. The epitome of autumn.

entries.name: Winter Court
entries.content:
The Winter Court is one of the seven courts in Prythian and the northernmost of the Seasonal Courts. The Court is made up of towering, exquisite palaces, full of roaring hearths and is bedecked in evergreens. Carved sleighs are the court's preferred method of transport, hauled by velvet-antlered reindeer whose splayed hooves are ideal for ice and snow. The Winter Court's forces are well trained, but they often rely on the great, white bears that stalk the realm for any unwanted visitors. The army includes these white bears, which wore armor during times of war, and used white foxes as couriers, the foxes carrying messages strapped to their embroidered vests.

The Winter Court's northern border is the Dawn Court, and its southern border is the Summer Court and Autumn Court.

The High Fae of the Winter Court have hair that is snow-white or as dark as the blackest night, skin ranging from moon pale to rich brown. They tend to wear fur-lined clothing. Their court has many species of Lesser Fae. One looks like long-limbed creatures that are shards of ice given form, tall enough they could place banners atop war tents. The fae of this court frown upon humans. They're more inclined to talk about their ope cruelty. This makes them look none other than evil, however one chooses to define evil. The Winter Court has free reign over winter solstice and autumn equinox months, and are strongest during that time. By and by, the fae of this court are sensible, chilled, dark, baleful, and what have you. They are the epitome of winter.

entries.name: Calanmai
entries.content:
Calanmai  or Fire Night, is a ceremony held in Prythian which signals the start of spring. On Fire Night, various celebrations occur, including lighting bonfires, the playing of drums, and the Great Rite. The crops depend upon the magic in the Great Rite on Fire Night. Each High Lord must perform the Great Rite, which consists in allowing powerful magic to enter their bodies and seize control of them, causing the High Lord to attempt to find the Maiden and have sex with her to release magic that will spread through the lands and allow crops to grow until the next Calanmai. In the Spring Court the Great Rite is performed in a sacred cave big enough to accommodate hundreds of Fae and a large number of bonfires. 

Smoke and magic often fill the atmosphere during the celebration where hundreds of male and female High Fae gather, many have sex that night as other dalliances will help the land too.

entries.name: Mate
entries.content:
A Mate is the name given to the individual with whom a special and very rare bond is shared, the Mating Bond. It is similar to the real-world idea of "soulmates", but much, much stronger.

The mating bond is described to appear as a link between the minds of the two Fae represented by different structures such as a bridge or string.

Members of the Fae species are able to sense their mates, but only if the other side is Fae. If their mate is mortal, then this sense will be dulled. Cassian suspected Nesta Archeron was his mate since she was still human.

A mating bond can reveal itself at different times depending on the couple. For some, it snaps into place right when the pair meet, but for others, it can be years before the bond is discovered.

When the mating bond is accepted it is higher than the bond between a regular married couple and is considered very sacred. When the mating bond snaps into place between a male and female, the female must offer the male food so they can be mated. Once a female has done this, she has accepted the mating bond. This can be done in a public mating ceremony or privately where only the couple is present and the female offers the male food

In a public mating ceremony, the mates swear their vows in front of a priestess and offer each other food. Then their friends and family bind their hands together with a length of black ribbon that remains until the mating is consummated

Once the mating bond is accepted, the couple falls into a state called "The Frenzy" that can last from a few days to several weeks.

It goes back to the beasts that the Fae once were, and is probably about ensuring that the male impregnates the female.

Some couples do not leave the house for a week. Males get so volatile that it can be dangerous for them to be in public. Males of reason and education have been known to shatter a room and attack other males, only because a male looked too long in the direction of his mate, too soon after their mating.

entries.name: Interacting With Fae
entries.content:
1. NEVER *give* your full name. A Fae may ask "May I have your name?" and to humans it sounds like they're just asking what our name is, but this allows them to own your name and thus own you. So either say a fake name or something along the lines of, "I am not in the habit of giving my name away, but I will tell you my name." But be careful because this implies you know the Fae rules and the Fae may become angry or more guarded.

2. Humans have become flippant about certain phrases to the point where they lose their original meaning, phrases like, "I love you," "Thank you," "You're welcome," "Please," "I promise to do x, y, z," etc. The Fae, however, are bound by their words. They mean every thing they say. Every. Thing. There are no technicalities, there are no loop holes (maybe for younger Fae who aren't used to dealing with humans that can promise something but aren't bound to that promise like the Fae is), and there are no minced words. Fae mean what they say and say what they mean. Think about the question, "May I have your name?" Again, to humans, this just sounds like an old/quirky/eccentric way to learn someone's name, but to the Fae, they are literally asking to have your name like you would ask your parent if you can have a pet. And if you answer with your actual name, that Fae now has your name. They own your name now, and thus they own you. The same thing with saying "Thank you," and "I'm sorry". The first phrase should only be used when something drastic has happened, like saving your life drastic. In place of saying "Thank you," you can say, "That's very kind of you," or something similar. And for the latter phrase, when you apologize to the Fae you better damn well mean it. You need to feel the apology in every bone of your body and be entirely sincere because if you aren't, the Fae will know and you will suffer.

3. Pay attention to wording. When it comes to technicalities and meanings and phrasings, Fae are like lawyers who read the fine print for fun. And once they've given their word on something, they can't go back on it. Lots of Humans try to trick Fae by using their words against them, which is one reason the Fae ignore or limit their dealings with Humans.

4. Substances that contain Iron are harmful to Fae. Even if the substance has Iron alloys in it, like Steel, it will still negatively affect the Fae. I've heard it burns them, or acts as a damper to their magic (this is questionable), so if you want to find favor with the Fae, don't wear anything Iron or have any Iron with you when meeting with the Fae. In this day and age, it can sometimes be difficult to know if something has Iron in it, and not all items that contain Iron are magnetic. Either the Iron content is too low or during the process of making the item the Iron was rendered nonmagnetic. If you happened upon a Fae and either forgot or didn't know that your jewelry, clothing, bag, etc. contained Iron, and depending on how the meeting goes, this would be an appropriate time to apologize for the offense, assuming that you truly are sorry. If you wish to be friends with the Fae, or at least tolerant neighbors, then getting rid of some, if not all Iron items in your house is a good place to start.

5.Speaking of Changelings, sometimes the Fae will exchange their sickly or ugly children for a beautiful Human child, forcing the Humans to raise a sickly child that may die or live a very difficult life. There is a way to reverse this and get the Human child back, but I don't remember how it goes. I've also heard that keeping an open pair of rusty scissors in the crib or bassinet of the sleeping baby will prevent the Fae from stealing the baby.

6.Also, never eat or drink anything offered by the Fae. Their food isn't meant for Human consumption and can cause anything from death to the Human being trapped by the Fae forever.

entries.name: Magic
entries.content:
Magic is an ability used by faerie. The abilities they can use often depend on their species, or if they were High Fae of Prythian, which court they belonged to. Magic has a scent, and it smells different depending on the fae and which court they are from.

 Magic is an innate ability of faerie. Besides being able to cast it, enchanted objects can be made. It can be countered and silenced by the placement of powerful spells or faebane.

Types of Magic: Bargains, Daemati (Ability to read, manipulate, and destroy someone's mind), Faelight, Glamouring, Healing, Seer (The ability to see future events through visions.), Shadowsinging (The ability to control shadows), Shapeshifting ( The ability to shift into animal or beast form.), Truth (The ability to detect truth and lies)

Court Specific Magic:
Winter Court- Ice Manipulation
Autumn Court- Fire Manipulation
Spring Court- Wind Manipulation
Summer Court- Water Manipulation
